title: Funeral for five-year-old girl Kumanjayi Little Baby confirmed by family

By Elsie Lange

Topic:Funerals and Memorial Services

A date and location has been set for Kumanjayi Little Baby's funeral. (ABC News: Marcus Kennedy)

The family of five-year-old girl Kumanjayi Little Baby, who was allegedly murdered in April, has set a date for her funeral.

Her grandfather has thanked the Alice Springs community for supporting the family and invited them to come together again at "our last farewell for our little granddaughter".

The funeral will take place on Saturday, August 15 at the Alice Springs Garden Cemetery.

Months on from the desperate search for five-year-old Kumanjayi Little Baby by hundreds of volunteers, her grandfather is inviting the community to come together once more for her funeral in Alice Springs later this month.

Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander readers are advised that this article includes the image of an Indigenous person who has died, used with the permission of their family.

Kumanjayi Little Baby went missing from Old Timers/Ilyperenye town camp, just south of the Alice Springs township, in late April, sparking one of the largest searches in Northern Territory police history.

Hundreds of community volunteers worked alongside police and emergency services to scour dense, grassy bushland for the five-year-old.

The search for Kumanjayi Little Baby in April lasted five days and involved hundreds of police and volunteers. (ABC News: Will Green)

Five days after she went missing, her remains were found 5 kilometres from the town camp, in the dry Todd River bed.

Her death triggered an outpouring of grief not just in Alice Springs but across the country, with vigils held in each state and territory, where thousands gathered in her favourite colour, pink, to pay their respects.

Mourners dressed in pink gathered at vigils for Kumanjayi Little Baby, where they paid tribute to the young girl. (ABC News: Marcus Kennedy)

Jefferson Lewis, 47, has since been charged with her murder and two other offences that cannot be published for legal reasons.

Since her death in April, Kumanjayi Little Baby's family has been in cultural grieving, known as sorry business.

Her funeral has now been set down to take place on August 15, with her family inviting members of the wider community to attend, and to wear her favourite colour again.

Five-year-old Kumanjayi Little Baby went missing from an Alice Springs town camp earlier this year.  (Supplied: NT Police)

Robin Japanangka Granites, a Warlpiri elder and Kumanjayi Little Baby's grandfather, told the ABC he wanted to thank the community again for their efforts to search for her, and for their outpouring of grief and support for his family.

"It was so nice of everyone getting together … the community of Alice Springs, who got together, everyone, not even saying who they were," he said.

"They are all as one with us, supporting, being out with us, during the hot days.

Robin Japanangka Granites says Kumanjayi Little Baby's life will be commemorated at the Alice Springs funeral. (ABC News: Xavier Martin)

Mr Granites said it had been a difficult time for the family, but they were rallying together for the funeral.

He used the Warlpiri word jintangka, meaning "all in one" or coming together.

"Thank you everyone who is coming to this get-together and this funeral to have our last farewell for our little granddaughter," he said.

"I thank you all for coming and it was really good of you, being all together, in one, jintangka … our little baby granddaughter of ours will be with Father in Heaven."

The news of Kumanjayi Little Baby's alleged murder rocked Australia. (ABC News: Xavier Martin)

The funeral for Kumanjayi Little Baby will take place at the Alice Springs Garden Cemetery at 10am to 1pm on Saturday, August 15.

The ABC understands another memorial is being planned for the Friday before the funeral, with further details around timing and location to come.
